memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate policy domains: the reference frame addresses participant-compensation fairness, calculation, and methods, while the compared frame addresses the stated boundaries and transferability of field-design knowledge. Neither frame contains a substantively matching claim from the other.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame provides this budgeting rule; the compared frame addresses the applicability of design knowledge.
relations.summary: Compensation budgets should reflect estimated session and preparation burden.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes compensation for required study travel.
relations.summary: Required travel time for face-to-face studies should be compensated.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes modality-independent payment for time spent in sessions.
relations.summary: Actual session time should be compensated regardless of research modality.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame addresses permissible payment methods.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame addresses when a compensation method must be finalized.
relations.summary: A proposal need not finalize the payment method when compensation equity is explained.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame defines rate parity across research modalities.
relations.summary: Face-to-face and remote studies should use the same base hourly rate when task burden is equal.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame states how participants judge compensation fairness.
relations.summary: Participants assess compensation fairness from total session, travel, and preparation burden.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame addresses the added burden of iterative participation and returning for multiple sessions.
relations.summary: Compensation should account for rescheduling iterations and repeated formative-session attendance.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes compensation for time spent before an error-driven early termination.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for invested time when prototype errors terminate a session early.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame records this calculation tendency.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to omit between-session preparation burden from iterative-study compensation calculations.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame links concise population and environment specification to reviewers' assessment of applicability.
relations.summary: Design knowledge should state its target population and usage environment because these define the results' generalization boundary.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame identifies and explains these operational conditions for applying guidance at another site.
relations.summary: Transferring field-design guidance requires matching workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational or authority conditions, not merely user characteristics.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame records this overgeneralization tendency.
relations.summary: The user tends to extend findings from one deployment site to all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines applicability through population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority conditions, and notes a tendency to overgeneralize findings across organizations.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers compensation based on session, preparation, travel, iteration, and interrupted-session burdens, alongside modality-neutral rates, cash availability, proposal-stage flexibility, fairness perceptions, and an observed omission tendency.
